editorial:
You wake up in a future where having more than one child is illegal, and seven identical sisters share one public identity to survive. Each sister gets one day of the week to live outside, but when Monday disappears, the others must break their careful routine to find her. Noomi Rapace plays all seven with different hair, clothes, and attitudes, so you always know who is who. The movie mixes sci-fi mystery with sharp action and a tense family drama, giving you a world that feels unfair but believable.

The action is fast and brutal, with chase scenes and fights that keep you on edge. The best part is watching the sisters argue, protect each other, and slowly uncover a bigger government secret. Some twists feel a little too convenient, and the story can get messy near the end, but the energy never drops. If you enjoy dystopian thrillers with strong female leads, this is a fun weekend pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: The twist is that Monday was not kidnapped at all; she made a secret deal with the government to protect her unborn baby. In the final showdown, the sisters confront Monday and the corrupt official, expose the child policy’s dark secret, and the surviving sisters finally get to live openly as themselves after years of hiding. The movie ends with hope as they step into the world without masks.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dystopian thrillers with strong female leads.
